+2 High School Pindaruch

A heritage rural school, established in 1945, upgraded to +2 — serving Class 6 to 12 in Pindaruch village, Darbhanga. Co-educational, Hindi and English medium, government-managed.

About the school

A heritage rural school, quietly modernising.

+2 High School Pindaruch is a historic educational institution located in the Keoti block of Darbhanga district, Bihar. Established in 1945, the school was originally recognised at the upper-primary, secondary and higher-secondary levels in the same year. After its recent upgrade to "Utkramit" (upgraded higher secondary) status, the school now serves students from Class 6 to Class 12.

The school is affiliated to the Bihar State Board and managed by the Department of Education, Government of Bihar. It is co-educational and offers instruction in both Hindi and English mediums. As of academic year 2025-26, the school has 1129 students (566 boys, 563 girls) taught by 41 teachers (28 male, 13 female), as per the public UDISE+ report card.

The school is included in the central PM SHRI schools list (2024-25) and runs several Bihar-government schemes — Unnayan Bihar smart-class content, daily Chetna Satra morning assembly, weekly Surakshit Shanivar safety activities, and Tarang art and sports festival participation.

This is a student project page, not the official school website. Verified information has been compiled from the UDISE+ 2025-26 public report card (school code 10130209009), the school's public Facebook page, and the 2011 Census village records. The photographs on this page are stock images from Google search, used for representative illustration only — not actual Pindaruch campus photos. See disclaimer and credits.

Morning assembly · Chetna Satra

The day opens with Chetna Satra — students leading students.

Every Bihar government school conducts a "Chetna Satra" (morning assembly) — a mandatory programme since August 2018. At Pindaruch, it is conducted rotationally by students of Class 6, 9 and 11, giving younger children a turn at public speaking and leadership early in school life.

01
Prayer — Day opens with a collective prayer.
02
News reading — A student presents the day's headlines.
03
Bihar Gaurav Gaan — The state anthem is sung collectively.
04
Quiz — A short interactive quiz closes the assembly.

Government schemes running at the school

Bihar and central schemes active on campus.

The school participates in several verified government schemes — central and Bihar-state level — aimed at digital learning, safety training, sports and culture.

PM SHRI · Central scheme

PM SHRI School (2024-25)

Included in the central Pradhan Mantri Schools for Rising India list — selected schools receive additional infrastructure and learning-quality support.

Bihar Education Department

Unnayan Bihar Smart Class

State programme launched 5 September 2019 — provides curriculum-aligned digital content via projector and screen, in 5646+ secondary/higher secondary schools.

Mandatory since Aug 2018

Chetna Satra / Prarthna Sabha

Mandatory daily morning assembly in all Bihar schools — prayer, news reading, Bihar Gaurav Gaan and quiz, led rotationally by students.

Mukhya Mantri Vidyalaya Suraksha Karyakram · 2025

Surakshit Shanivar

Bagless Safe Saturday — weekly Saturday activities training students in disaster response, fire safety, earthquake preparedness and basic first-aid.

Bihar state festival

Tarang — Art and Sports Festival

Annual inter-school art and sports festival, including traditional Indian games. Students from Pindaruch participate each year.

TCIL empanelled

ICT Lab (TCIL)

The school is in the TCIL empanelled ICT-instructor list — meaning a computer instructor is provided for digital-literacy classes.

Pindaruch village is in Keotirunway block (also referred to as Keoti in UDISE+ records), with pincode 847306. The village has two government schools, a Sanskrit College, a Panchayat Bhawan, a Cricket Club, six temples and two mosques. The school is on SH-75 (Darbhanga–Kamtaul road), near the Pindaruch railway crossing.

Legal · 01

Privacy Policy

Last updated: 14 September 2026 · Applies to: this static student project page

1. Overview

This is a static, read-only student project page hosted on GitHub Pages. It is not the official website of +2 High School Pindaruch. The page does not have a backend, does not run any server-side code, and does not store any user information.

2. Data we collect

This page does not collect any personal data from visitors. Specifically:

  • No cookies are set by this page.
  • No analytics or tracking scripts are loaded — there is no Google Analytics, no Facebook Pixel, no Hotjar, no Mixpanel, or any similar service.
  • No form submissions are processed. There is no contact form on the page.
  • No login or account system exists.
  • No browser fingerprinting is performed.
  • No IP address is logged by this page (GitHub Pages logs server-side IPs, but those are not accessible to or controlled by me — see GitHub's own privacy policy for that).

3. Third-party resources loaded

The page loads only the following third-party resources, none of which track the visitor:

  • Google Fonts (fonts.googleapis.com) — Fraunces, IBM Plex Sans, IBM Plex Mono. These fonts are loaded as static CSS and font files. Google may log the request as part of its standard CDN operation, but no analytics ID is sent from this page to Google.

No third-party JavaScript libraries, no CDN scripts, no iframes, no embedded videos, no social-media embeds are used. All three photographs are embedded directly inside the HTML as base64 data URIs, so no separate image requests are made.

4. Information shown on the page

The page displays the following public information about the school:

  • School name, U-DISE code, address, block, district, pincode — all sourced from the public UDISE+ report card.
  • School's public phone number (+91 96311 71889) — sourced from the school's public Facebook page.
  • Student and teacher counts — sourced from the public UDISE+ 2025-26 report card.
  • Village population and literacy figures — sourced from the public Census 2011 village records.
  • Government scheme names — verified as real programmes via public news sources and Bihar government portals.

No personal information about any individual student, teacher, parent or community member is published on this page. No photographs of identifiable individuals are used; where photographs of people appear, faces are blurred beyond recognition.

5. Children's privacy

This page is about a school and may be visited by students, parents and teachers. Because no personal data is collected from any visitor — adult or child — there is no COPPA, GDPR-K or equivalent child-privacy obligation triggered. However, I have voluntarily chosen to blur all faces in photographs and to not publish any student names.

6. Your choices

Since no data is collected, there is nothing for you to opt out of. If you use a private browser, block third-party fonts, or disable JavaScript, the page will still work — only the smooth-scroll and reveal animations will fall back to default browser behaviour.

7. Changes to this policy

If the page is updated in a way that changes the privacy behaviour, this document will be updated too. The "Last updated" date at the top will reflect the change.

8. Contact

This is an unofficial student project. There is no official contact email published here. For corrections, please open an issue on the GitHub repository hosting this page. For any matter relating to the actual school, please contact the school office directly at the address shown on the contact section of the profile page.

9. License of this document

This Privacy Policy document, like the rest of the project source code, is released under the MIT License. See the MIT License section for the full text.

4. Visual assets

All SVG icons (location pin, clock, book, power bolt, etc.) and the brand mark used as the favicon are original hand-coded artwork created by me. They are released into the public domain under CC0 — no attribution required.

The three photographs embedded as base64 data URIs in this file are stock images sourced from Google search, used here for representative illustration only. They are not actual photographs of the Pindaruch campus. Where faces appear, they are blurred beyond recognition. These photographs are not licensed for commercial reuse — before publishing this page publicly, I should replace them with my own campus photographs taken with the school's permission.

5. Code and libraries

This page uses no external JavaScript or CSS libraries — no jQuery, no Bootstrap, no Tailwind, no Alpine, no HTMX. Everything is hand-written vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The page loads exactly one external stylesheet (Google Fonts) and zero external scripts.

The smooth-scroll and reveal-on-scroll animations are implemented using the browser-native IntersectionObserver API and scroll-behavior: smooth CSS property. The mobile menu uses native CSS transitions. The legal overlay pages use pure CSS :target selectors — no JavaScript is required to open or close them. The prefers-reduced-motion media query is respected throughout.

6. Tools used to build this page

  • A plain text editor (I wrote the HTML/CSS/JS by hand).
  • Google Fonts API for the font files.
  • Python's Pillow library (PIL) to compress the photographs and convert them to base64 data URIs.
  • The agent-browser CLI for testing the page across viewport sizes during development.

7. Special thanks

I acknowledge:

  • The team that maintains the UDISE+ public report card system — a remarkable national school-data resource that made the verified numbers on this page possible.
  • The Census of India team for the village-level data.
  • The Bihar Education Department and SCERT Bihar for the scheme documentation publicly available.
  • The open-source community for maintaining browser-native Web APIs that make frameworks unnecessary for projects like this.
  • The school's own teaching staff whose work this page attempts to represent in good faith.

A heritage rural school established 1945 in Pindaruch village, Keoti block, Darbhanga. Class 6 to 12, with Science, Arts and Commerce streams at the +2 level.
